formula: log(apps) ~ d93 + bowl + btitle + finfour + avg500 + stufac + top25 + (1 | school)
notes: RESPONSE INFERRED: the page names no model. Universities (school) observed in 1992 and 1993 (d93); "The 'athletic success' variables are for the year prior to the enrollment and academic data", and the table carries first differences of lapps, bowl, btitle, finfour, avg500, stufac and top25 (the c-prefixed columns), so the term project (Used in Text page 697, Ch. 19) relates the change in log applications to athletic success and academic quality. Rendered in levels with a random intercept on the university, Gaussian on log(apps). avg500 is (ver500 + mth500)/2, so its parts are ignored; bball is btitle or finfour; lapps_1 is the lag. Hand check #162: stands; the source fits no model, so the school intercept stays the reader's proposal (59 universities of two years each).

formula: log(avgsal) ~ bs + lenroll + lstaff + lunch + bsbar + lenrollbar + lstaffbar + lunchbar + (1 | distid)
notes: The page holds only the columns (no description, not marked as used in the text). They are elem94_95's Michigan elementary schools (schid, one row each) within districts (distid), whose page says the data "can be used to study the salary-benefits tradeoff, as in Chapter 4": log(avgsal) on the benefits-salary ratio bs with lenroll, lstaff and lunch (recalled from Wooldridge's Ch. 4 and 9 exercises). This table adds the within-district averages bsbar, lunchbar, lenrollbar and lstaffbar, the terms of Wooldridge's correlated random effects (Mundlak) approach for a cluster sample (Ch. 14, recalled, not read), so the formula carries them beside a random district intercept. bs is avgben/avgsal, so avgben is ignored; enroll and staff are the raw columns of the logged covariates. Hand check #162: Imbens and Wooldridge's cemmap slides (PDF p. 335) fit xtreg lavgsal bs lstaff lenroll lunch bsbar lstaffbar lenrollbar lunchbar, re cluster(distid) on these 1,848 schools of 537 districts, so the model is published. Their ordinary random-effects fit without the district means (PDF pp. 330-331) has the same response and grouping, so it files no row.

formula: log(salary) ~ pubindx + top20phd + female + exper + I(exper^2) + assoc + prof + chair + factor(year) + (1 | id)
notes: Help page (Notes): "an unbalanced panel data set in the sense that as many as three years of data are available for each faculty member"; FE or FD would control away productivity, so "Pooled OLS regression with 'cluster robust' standard errors seems more natural", to measure "the effect of productivity on salary" and "the return to having a degree from a top 20 Ph.D. program" (Baser and Pema 2003; not used in the text). Pooled OLS only, so the faculty member (id) is a random intercept (Panels ruling). The terms are proposed from the page: publication index, top-20 Ph.D., sex, experience and its square, rank (assistant the reference), chair and year; the university dummies (osu to illinois) stay out of the formula. lsalary, expersq, the year dummies and pubindx's square, zero indicator and log are derived. Hand check #162: stands; Baser and Pema (2003) fit pooled OLS and fixed effects on a richer specification, so the faculty intercept stays the reader's proposal (262 faculty members of three years each).

formula: lweekinc ~ educ + (1 | state) + (1 | state:puma)
notes: Census 2000 microdata provided by Abadie (Used in Text pages 452-453, Ch. 13). Hand check #162: Wooldridge's problem 7 of chapter 14 (7th ed., p. 485) regresses lweekinc on educ alone and compares standard errors clustered by puma and by state, so the response and fixed part are documented and exper and expersq are ignored. Workers repeat within Public Use Microdata Areas inside states; puma codes repeat across states (610 codes, 269 in several states), so the area term is state:puma, nested in state (2,024 areas of 1 to 54 workers), and the 51 states group as an exhaustive set of many units. Both intercepts stay the reader's proposal, low.

formula: soyhec ~ cornpix + soypix + (1 | county)
notes: Second response of the Battese, Harter and Fuller (1988) data over the same county grouping; see model 1. BHF predict the county areas of both crops from both pixel counts with a random county effect, as the registry's rabe_hesketh cropareas.dta row 2 records from its hand check; not read in the paper here, so medium. Hand check #162: stands; agridat's battese.survey example (m4) reproduces this model of Battese, Harter and Fuller (1988, p. 33) without Hardin's outlying segment (county 12, soyhec 29.46), a subset fit kept on the whole table. Battese's (1982) single-predictor fits, cornhec ~ cornpix and soyhec ~ soypix, have the responses and grouping of models 1 and 2, so they file no row.

formula: murdrate ~ execs + I(ave(execs, countyid, FUN = function(x) c(NA, head(x, -1)))) + percblack + percmale + perc1019 + perc2029 + factor(year) + (1 | countyid)
notes: Help page: county panel 1980-1996 of murders, murder arrests and executions with county demographics (countyid "1000*statefips + countyfips"; Used in Text pages 16, 58, 431, 457). Wooldridge's exercises on COUNTYMURDERS (recalled, not read) relate the murder rate to executions by pooled OLS, first differences and fixed effects, with year effects, the demographic shares. The lag of execs, which no column holds, is written as its within-county expression. FE and FD only, so the county is a random intercept (Panels ruling). murders is the count behind murdrate; arrests, arrestrate and execrate are alternate measures; lpopul is log(popul); statefips and countyfips make up countyid. Hand check #162: Wooldridge's C16 of chapter 13 (7th ed., p. 458) includes the previous year's executions; the lag needs the rows sorted by countyid and year, as stored (2,197 counties of 17 years each). published_model stays no: the exercise asks for pooled OLS and first differences.

formula: log(crime) ~ d78 + clrprc1 + clrprc2 + (1 | district)
notes: Help page: "These data are for the years 1972 and 1978 for 53 police districts in Norway" (Eide 1994, Tables A3 and A6). Wooldridge (Used in Text pages 464-465, recalled, not read) fits the distributed lag of log crime on the clear-up percentages of the prior year and of two years before by first differencing, the change in log(crime) on the changes in clrprc1 and clrprc2, and an exercise (pages 477-478) uses their average avgclr. FD only, so the district is a random intercept (Panels ruling); d78 carries the period intercept and codes year. The c-prefixed columns are the first differences. Hand check #162: stands; the 53 police districts group as an exhaustive set of many units, each observed in 1972 and 1978, and the source's first differences leave the district intercept the reader's proposal.

formula: log(crmrte) ~ lpolpc + ldensity + lwcon + lwser + lwtrd + factor(year) + (1 | county)
notes: Hand check #162: Stavrakoudis's panel tutorial (stavrakoudis.econ.uoi.gr/stavrakoudis/learnr/panel-OLS-FE-RE.html) fits re_c, plm(lcrmrte ~ lpolpc + ldensity + lwcon + lwser + lwtrd + d82 + d83 + d84 + d85 + d86 + d87, model = 'random'), on these 630 rows of 90 counties, which replaces the reader's random-intercept rendering of Wooldridge's Example 13.9 (Heiss, Using R for Introductory Econometrics, Script 13.7: first differences of log(crmrte) on the year dummies, lprbarr, lprbconv, lprbpris, lavgsen and lpolpc). Cornwell and Trumbull (1994) North Carolina panel, a copy of rabe_hesketh crime.dta. The year dummies are factor(year); the raw columns, the other logs and the c-prefixed first differences are ignored.

formula: totfatrte ~ bac08 + bac10 + perse + sbprim + sbsecon + sl70plus + gdl + perc14_24 + unem + vehicmilespc + factor(year) + (1 | state)
notes: Help page: the 48 continental states (state, alphabetical) 1980-2004 (Freeman 2007, "Drunk Driving Legislation and Traffic Fatalities: New Evidence on BAC 08 Laws"); Used in Text: "not used, but see page 695". Wooldridge's Ch. 13 and 14 exercises on DRIVING (recalled, not read) regress totfatrte on year dummies, bac08, bac10, perse, sbprim, sbsecon, sl70plus, gdl, perc14_24, unem and vehicmilespc by pooled OLS, first differences and fixed effects. FE and FD only, so the state is a random intercept (Panels ruling). The other fatality counts and rates are alternate responses; seatbelt is coded by sbprim and sbsecon, sl70, sl75 and slnone are summed into sl70plus, and d80 to d04 code year. Hand check #162: stands; the 48 continental states group as an exhaustive set of many units (25 years each). Wooldridge's C13 of chapter 14 (5th ed.) fits pooled OLS and state fixed effects, so the state intercept stays the reader's proposal.

formula: log(uclms) ~ ez + factor(year) + (1 | city)
notes: Indiana cities 1980-1988 with and without an enterprise zone (Papke 1994, the source of ezanders). Wooldridge Example 13.8 (Used in Text page 470, recalled, not read): log(uclms) on year effects and ez with a city effect, estimated by first differences; the exercise on page 504 uses fixed effects. FD and FE only, so the city is a random intercept (Panels ruling), Gaussian on the log of the claims count. c1 to c22 are the city dummies, d81 to d88 code year, and luclms, guclms and cez are the log, its change and the change in ez. Hand check #162: stands; 22 cities of nine years each. The table equals rabe_hesketh ezunem.dta in its 37 columns, to which that file adds four derived ones.

formula: trmgpa ~ spring + sat + hsperc + female + black + white + frstsem + tothrs + crsgpa + season + (1 | id)
notes: Students (id, "student identifier") of GPA2's university over the fall and spring terms (term, spring). The examples on pages 246-248 fit cumgpa on the spring term alone (Heiss, Using R for Introductory Econometrics, Script 7.7: lm(cumgpa ~ female*(sat+hsperc+tothrs), data = gpa3, subset = (spring==1))), with no repeated student. The Ch. 13 exercise on page 478 (recalled, not read) treats the student-athletes' two terms as a panel and asks whether athletes do worse in the term their sport is in season: trmgpa on spring, sat, hsperc, female, black, white, frstsem, tothrs, crsgpa and season by pooled OLS and first differences. Pooled OLS and FD only, so the student is a random intercept (Panels ruling). cumgpa is an alternate response, the c-prefixed columns are first differences, and term is coded by spring. Hand check #162: stands; Wooldridge's C7 of chapter 13 (5th ed.) fits pooled OLS and first differences, so the student intercept stays the reader's proposal (366 student-athletes of two terms each).

formula: log(scrap) ~ d88 + d89 + grant + grant_1 + (1 | fcode)
notes: Michigan manufacturing firms (fcode, "firm code number") 1987-1989 (Holzer et al. 1993). Wooldridge Example 14.1 (Used in Text pages 486-487, recalled, not read): fixed effects of log(scrap) on d88, d89, grant and the lagged grant grant_1; earlier examples difference 1987 and 1988, and Example 15.10 (Heiss, Using R for Introductory Econometrics, Script 15.6) fits plm(log(scrap) ~ hrsemp | grant, model = "fd", data = jtrain.p) with pdata.frame(index = c("fcode","year")). Hand check #162: Stavrakoudis's panel tutorial (stavrakoudis.econ.uoi.gr/stavrakoudis/learnr/panel-OLS-FE-RE.html) fits re_j, plm(lscrap ~ grant + grant_1 + d88 + d89, model = 'random'), this formula, on the 162 rows of the 54 firms reporting scrap. UCLA's Example 10.4 with union and Varghese's lecture with tothrs fit the same response and grouping, so they file no row. rework is an alternate response; year is coded by d88 and d89; the logs of other columns and the c-prefixed first differences are derived.

formula: lowbrth ~ d90 + afdcprc + lphypc + lbedspc + lpcinc + lpopul + (1 | state)
notes: Hand check #162: Rodriguez's GLM course (grodri.github.io/glms/r/c8s2) fits lmer(lowbrth ~ d90 + afdcprc + lphypc + lbedspc + lpcinc + lpopul + (1 | stateabb), REML = FALSE) on these 100 rows of 50 states, 1987 and 1990, which replaces the reader's proposal with afdcprc's square (the help's notes on pooled OLS and first differences). stateabb holds the same groups as state; infmort is the alternate response; year aliases d90; the c* columns are first differences and afdcpsq the square; pcinc, physicpc, bedspc and popul are the raw forms of the logged regressors.

formula: math4 ~ lrexpp + lrexpp_1 + lenrol + lunch + factor(year) + (1 | distid)
notes: Wooldridge pages 479-480 and 505-506 use these Michigan district panels (Papke) in computer exercises; recalled, not checked: math4 on year dummies, log real spending per pupil and its lag, log enrollment and lunch, by first differences and fixed effects, no random-effects fit. Rendered per this pass's panel ruling with a district random intercept (550 districts, 1992-1998; 1992 has no lagged spending). intid, the intermediate school district that nests the districts, is not fitted. math7, drop and grad are alternate outcomes; the y* dummies code year; the other l*, g*, c*, *_1, *sq and *92 columns are transforms of spending, the foundation grant, enrollment, lunch and math4. Hand check #162: stands; Wooldridge's C8 of chapter 14 (5th ed.) fits pooled OLS and fixed effects, so the district intercept stays the reader's proposal (550 districts of seven years each).

formula: math4 ~ lexppp + lunch + (1 | dcode)
notes: The help's notes: a simple regression of math4 on lexppp gives a negative coefficient and controlling for lunch makes the spending coefficient positive (Wooldridge page 18), OLS on Michigan elementary schools (bcode, one row each) in 2001. Schools repeat within districts (dcode), rendered as a district random intercept per the repeating-cluster ruling though the source treats schools as independent. read4 is the alternate response; expend, exppp and lexpend are other forms of spending; lenroll is log(enroll), which is unused. Hand check #162: stands; 1,823 schools in 564 districts of 1 to 170 schools, 246 with several.

formula: math4 ~ pctsgle + lmedinc + free + (1 | dcode) + (1 | zipcode)
notes: Wooldridge (6th edition) pages 100, 145-146 and 198 use these 229 Michigan schools in computer exercises; recalled, not checked: math4 on pctsgle (percent of children in the school's zipcode not in married-couple families), then adding lmedinc and free, by OLS. Schools repeat within districts (dcode), rendered as a district random intercept per the repeating-cluster ruling; zipcode, the unit of the census columns (medinc, totchild, married, single, pctsgle), also repeats, a second grouping factor crossed with dcode. read4 is the alternate response; lunch is free + reduced; lenroll and lexppp are logs of enroll and exppp. Hand check #162: 83 ZIP codes of 1 to 8 schools, 17 spanning several districts; math4 varies within 61 ZIP codes and 36 of the 47 districts.

formula: mrdrte ~ exec + unem + factor(year) + (1 | id)
notes: Wooldridge pages 480, 505 and 548 use this state panel (1987, 1990, 1993) in computer exercises; recalled, not checked: mrdrte on year dummies, exec and unem by pooled OLS and first differences, then fixed effects and an IV version, no random-effects fit; rendered per this pass's panel ruling with a state random intercept on id. state is the postal code of id; d90 and d93 code year; the c* columns are first differences and their lags. Hand check #162: stands; the random-effects fits found drop the year effects (a UCL lecture mirrored on Scribd, unread; a Stack Exchange question's xtreg mrdrte exec unem, re on the 153 rows), and neither is a published model, so the formula stays the reader's proposal (51 states of three years each).

formula: winperc ~ prerpi + postrpi_1 + (1 | team)
notes: Not used in the text; the help's notes ask whether the preseason RPI helps predict performance (such as win percentage or making the NCAA tournament) once the previous year's post-season RPI is controlled for, by multiple regression, with probit or logit for the tournament indicator (row 2), and say coaching experience can be added. Teams repeat over seasons, rendered as a team random intercept per this pass's panel ruling. wins and losses give winperc; postrpi is this season's post-season rank, an outcome; conference, power5, recruitrank, postrpi_2 and coachexper are unused; year is the season. Hand check #162: stands; 84 teams of four seasons each.

formula: tourney ~ prerpi + postrpi_1 + (1 | team)
notes: Row 1's reading with the tournament indicator as response; the help's notes name probit or logit for it, so the logit of the contract's rule stands. Hand check #162: stands; tourney varies within 58 of the 84 teams.

formula: pctstck ~ choice + prftshr + female + age + educ + finc25 + finc35 + finc50 + finc75 + finc100 + finc101 + wealth89 + stckin89 + irain89 + (1 | id)
notes: Wooldridge page 506 (a chapter 14 computer exercise, recalled, not checked): some rows are spouses of one family (id), a cluster sample with clusters of at most two; pctstck is regressed by OLS on these regressors ignoring the clustering, then with cluster-robust errors and family fixed effects (Papke 2004, National Longitudinal Survey of Mature Women). Rendered per this pass's panel ruling with a family random intercept. pctstck holds three ordered codes (0 mostly bonds, 50 mixed, 100 mostly stocks) fitted as linear, hence gaussian. pyears, married and black are unused. Hand check #162: stands; 171 families, 23 of them couples, pctstck varying within 4 of the couples, a weak grouping.

formula: lcriv ~ I(ave(pris, state, FUN = function(x) c(NA, head(x, -1)))) + log(incpc) + unem + log(polpc) + black + metro + ag0_14 + ag15_17 + ag18_24 + ag25_34 + (1 | state)
notes: Hand check #162: Lal's panel notes (apoorvalal.github.io/notebook/causal_inference_notes/2-Panel.html) replicate Levitt (1996) by plm(log(criv) ~ lag_pris + log(incpc) + unem + log(polpc) + black + metro + ag0_14 + ag15_17 + ag18_24 + ag25_34, model = 'random') on Stata's prison.dta, lag_pris the previous year's pris within state, 663 rows (each state's first year lacks the lag). This replaces the reader's rendering of Wooldridge's chapter 16 exercise after Levitt (first differences of log violent crime on gpris and the controls' changes, with year dummies, then final1 and final2 instrumenting gpris). The lag needs the rows sorted by state and year, as stored (50 states and DC, 1980-1993). lcriv is log(criv), criv per 1,000 residents here and per 100,000 in Lal's file, which shifts only the intercept; crip and its forms are the property-crime alternate response; lpris, the y81-y93 dummies, year, govelec, final1 and final2 are unused.

formula: lrent ~ y90 + lpop + lavginc + pctstu + (1 | city)
notes: Wooldridge pages 160, 477 and 503-504 (computer exercises, recalled, not checked): log(rent) on y90, log(pop), log(avginc) and pctstu, pooled over 1980 and 1990 by OLS, then first differences and fixed effects; rendered per this pass's panel ruling with a city random intercept (64 college towns). The help's notes also sketch housing demand and supply equations for ltothsg with pctstu as instrument (ltothsg and lrnthsg are alternate responses). The c* columns are 1980-1990 changes; rent, pop and avginc are the raw forms of the logs; year aliases y90; lenroll is log(enroll). Hand check #162: stands; 64 college towns, 1980 and 1990.

formula: math4 ~ lavgrexpp + lunch + lenrol + factor(year) + (1 | schid)
notes: The help's notes: school-level data of Papke (2005), unbalanced; the usual RE and FE methods apply directly, and Computer Exercise 17 of chapter 14 walks through the correlated random effects version of the Hausman test (Wooldridge page 491). The regressors are recalled from Papke's model (math4 on the log of real spending averaged over the current and previous year, lunch, log enrollment and year effects), not checked. distid, the school's district, is a higher level not fitted; y93-y98 code year; exppp, rexpp and lrexpp are other spending forms and enrol the raw enrollment; found is unused. Hand check #162: stands; Wooldridge's C17 of chapter 14 (7th ed., p. 491) asks for this random-effects model, year dummies included, on the complete cases (7,274 rows of 1,773 schools; lavgrexpp is missing for every school in 1993). Its correlated random effects variants (part v, with and without the year dummies' means) have the same response and grouping, so they file no row.
